before.stem: ww A71 year old man walks into ED following a fall. He is complaining of neck pain and weakness affecting his upper limbs only. Which of the following spinal cord lesions is most likely:
options: Complete cord transection (x) Brown-Sequard syndrome 4% Vv) Central cord syndrome 28%
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: Central cord syndrome (CCS) is marked by a disproportionately greater impairment of motor function in the upper extremities than in the lower ones, as well as by bladder dysfunction and a variable amount of sensory loss below the injury level. Vv Spinal Cord Tracts

before.stem: ww The blood supply to the frontal lobe is primarily supplied by which of the following arteries:
options: Anterior cerebral artery (x) Middle cerebral artery 4%

warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The blood supply to the frontal lobe is from the anterior cerebral artery (supplying the medial surface of the primary motor cortex which controls the lower limb) and the middle cerebral artery (supplying the lateral surface of the primary motor cortex which controls the face and upper limb). : Vv Frontal Lobe ANATOMY / CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM
